sources.title: Mark Goresky, Lecture Notes on Sheaves and Perverse Sheaves, version of June 26, 2026
sources.locator: Sections read in the full 168-page PDF (text extracted with MuPDF): 1 pp. 3-10, especially 1(a) sheaves and 1(d) local systems and locally constant sheaves pp. 5-7 and 1(g) extension by zero p. 7; 2 pp. 10-13, especially 2.1-2.3 simplicial sheaves and their cochain cohomology pp. 10-11 and 2.5-2.7 fine, flabby and injective sheaves pp. 12-13; 3 pp. 13-15, especially 3.1 injective resolutions, 3.2 cohomology as a right derived functor and 3.3 quasi-isomorphism invariance; 4.1 and 4.4 pp. 16-18 Godement resolution and the Cech comparison; 5.1-5.4 pp. 18-20 the sheaf of chains and Borel-Moore homology; 6.1 and 7 pp. 20-23 homotopy, injectives and the derived category; 8.1-8.2 pp. 24-25 stratifications and the frontier axiom; 8.3-8.5 pp. 25-29 normal slice, link and local structure; 9.1-9.4 pp. 30-32 constructible sheaves and the bounded constructible derived category; 11.1-11.2 pp. 34-36 Verdier duality and the Borel-Moore sheaf of chains.

contents.name: 1(d), pp. 5-7: local systems as leaf spaces of locally constant sheaves, trivialization over contractible open subsets, simplicial homology with local coefficients
2.1-2.3, pp. 10-11: simplicial sheaves, chains with values in a simplicial sheaf, the cochain complex and its cohomology
2.5-2.7 with 3.1-3.2, pp. 12-15: fine, flabby and injective sheaves; injective resolutions; cohomology of a sheaf and of a complex as a right derived functor of global sections
3.3, pp. 14-15: a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of sheaves induces isomorphisms on cohomology over every open subset
4.1 and 4.4, pp. 16-18: Godement resolution, flabby sheaves and the comparison with Cech cohomology
contents.reason: This pair uses injective and flasque resolutions only; the Godement and Cech models and their comparison are already published on the prerequisite page sheaf-cohomology-cech-cohomology-and-comparison.

contents.name: 5.1-5.4, pp. 18-20: the sheaf of chains, Borel-Moore homology and spaces of finite type
contents.reason: Compactly supported and Borel-Moore sheaf calculus belongs to the later compact-support-sheaf-calculus and analytic-derived-six-operations-and-duality pairs of this frontier, not to the constructibility foundations pair.

contents.name: 6.1 and 7, pp. 20-23: homotopy of complexes, injective resolutions and the derived category; f_* preserves injectives; hypercohomology as a right derived functor
8.1-8.2, pp. 24-25: a stratification is a locally finite decomposition into locally closed smooth submanifolds satisfying the frontier axiom, with connected strata; Whitney condition B
8.3-8.5, pp. 25-29: normal slice, link, local structure theorem, tubular neighbourhoods and controlled vector fields
contents.reason: Whitney regularity, conical local structure and control data are the subject of the complex-algebraic-stratified-topology pair (order 1809) and are not needed for the definitional foundations of this pair.

contents.name: 9.1-9.2, pp. 30-31: constructible sheaves, cohomologically constructible complexes, algebraic constructibility for complex varieties and the bounded constructible derived category D_c^b
9.3-9.4, pp. 31-32: finite generation of hypercohomology on compact constructible complexes; constructibility of i_*i^* and j_*j^*; RHom of constructible complexes
contents.reason: Finiteness of cohomology and preservation of constructibility under pushforward are supplied locally by the later stratified-topology and incidence-model pairs; this foundations pair only fixes the definition and the triangulated closure.

contents.name: 11.1-11.2, pp. 34-36: Verdier duality, the dualizing complex, and the Borel-Moore sheaf of chains as the dual of the constant sheaf via the flabby sheaf of singular cochains
contents.reason: Verdier duality and chain-sheaf duality are constructed in the later analytic-derived-six-operations-and-duality pair (order 1813) and in the compact-support pair; they are not premises of the constructibility definition here.

sources.title: Joseph Bernstein and Valery Lunts, Equivariant Sheaves and Functors, Lecture Notes in Mathematics 1578, Part I (Derived category and functors)
sources.locator: Part I of the retrieved excerpt, PDF pp. 1-11 (book pages 1-10): 0.2 equivariant sheaves and the abelian category Sh_G(X) pp. 1-2; 1.1-1.2 the bounded derived category D^b(X), truncations and realization of its objects by bounded complexes of injective sheaves pp. 4-5; 1.3 tensor product and internal Hom p. 5; 1.4.1-1.4.3 composition and adjunctions of the six functors pp. 5-6; 1.4.4 proper f_! = f_* and 1.4.5 the exact triangles of open and closed subsets p. 6.

contents.name: 1.1-1.2, PDF pp. 4-5: the bounded derived category D^b(X) of sheaves, its truncations, and the realization of every object of D^b(X) by a bounded complex of injective sheaves for nice spaces
1.3, PDF p. 5: tensor product and internal Hom on D^b(X)
contents.reason: Derived tensor and internal Hom are constructed in the later analytic-derived-six-operations-and-duality pair; this pair only needs the injective model of the derived category.

contents.name: 1.4.1-1.4.3, PDF pp. 5-6: composition of the six functors and the adjunctions f^* adjoint f_*, f_! adjoint f^!
1.4.4, PDF p. 6: the canonical morphism f_! -> f_* is an isomorphism for proper f
1.4.5, PDF p. 6: the exact triangles of an open subset i_!i^*F -> F -> j_*j^*F and j_!j^!F -> F -> i_*i^*F, with i^! = i_* and j_! extension by zero
0.2, PDF pp. 1-2: G-equivariant sheaves and the abelian category Sh_G(X)
contents.reason: Equivariant sheaf theory is the subject of the later equivariant-constructible-perverse-foundations pair (order 1818); the nonequivariant constructions of this pair do not use it.

sources.locator: Sections read in the full 168-page PDF: 1(d) pp. 5-7 local systems and trivialization over contractible opens; 1(g) p. 7 extension by zero of a twisted local system on the complement of the Alexander horned sphere; 9.2 p. 30 algebraic constructibility and D_c^b; 11.2 pp. 35-36 the Borel-Moore sheaf of chains.

contents.name: 1(d), pp. 5-7: contractible open subsets trivialize a locally constant sheaf; locally constant sheaves have simplicial homology
1(g), p. 7: extension by zero of a twisted local system on the complement of the Alexander horned sphere
contents.reason: This pathology illustrates nonconstructible extension by zero; the example's line computation uses only the constant coefficient case and the published open/closed sequence.

contents.name: 9.2, p. 30: algebraic constructibility for complex varieties and the bounded constructible derived category D_c^b
11.2, pp. 35-36: the Borel-Moore sheaf of chains as the dual of the constant sheaf after replacing it by the flabby sheaf of singular cochains
contents.reason: Chain-level duality is not used by the point and line computations of this example; it belongs to the later duality pair of this frontier.
